insights.insight: Crinkl has processed $4.83M in cryptographically verified purchase GMV across 91,727 receipts — deterministic proof of completed transactions, not modeled intent. That base is large enough to run meaningful category and brand-level analyses against real shopper behavior.

Grocery and restaurants account for 2,557 of the 5,137 receipts in the trailing 14 days, with Walmart, Kroger, Safeway, Costco, and Aldi all appearing in the top-brand window — the panel skews toward high-frequency, replenishment-category spending where recency and frequency signals matter most.

Three new brand-list entries across four days (McDonald's Oct 12, Lowe's Oct 15, H-E-B Oct 16) and an 18th active metro area confirmed Oct 16 indicate the panel is actively broadening beyond its origin markets — a relevant check for brands evaluating whether coverage is sufficient for regional or national campaign planning.

insights.topic: Daily receipt velocity and structural rhythm
insights.insight: The panel is running at a structural pace of 328–398 verified receipts per day, with a consistent late-UTC burst window that accounts for a material share of daily volume — marketers modeling reach or frequency caps should account for this intraday skew rather than assuming uniform distribution.

After 30 consecutive snapshots above 1.0x acceleration, the growth multiplier has posted two consecutive readings at 0.999x — not yet a confirmed deceleration given the provisional state of the current UTC day, but the first observable inflection in the growth trend and worth watching against the next closed-day reading.

insights.topic: DKIM vendor set extends to digital goods
insights.insight: Receipt verification now spans Amazon, Stripe, Paddle, Gumroad, and SaaS vendors alongside physical retail — meaning the panel captures digital purchase behavior (software, subscriptions, creator economy) that traditional loyalty or POS-based panels miss entirely.
